subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- October 17, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - October 17, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS Community,

As we continue to move forward with our mission to provide a user-friendly, privacy-focused Linux distribution, we're excited to share some recent updates and milestones achieved by our community members.

In the past week, we've seen a flurry of activity across various projects, including the AcreetionOS GitLab instance. Our community members have been working tirelessly to improve the distribution, and their efforts are starting to bear fruit. One notable achievement is the initial commit of acreetion-surf v2.0.0, which marks a significant milestone in our ongoing efforts to enhance the user experience.

Meanwhile, on the development front, cobra3282000 has made some notable contributions to the Calamares project. Their work on fixing the displaymanager job crash and implementing Wayland session as the default desktop environment will undoubtedly improve the overall user experience. Additionally, they've also made significant progress on the lmm-ai project, which aims to bring AI-powered features to our distribution.

Natalie, our co-lead developer, has been actively working on the ember-vulkan project, which promises to bring improved graphics performance to our users. Her dedication to pushing the boundaries of what's possible with AcreetionOS is truly inspiring.

In other news, the GNOME Project has announced the availability of GNOME OS Preview, a new operating system that shares some similarities with our own AcreetionOS. While we're excited to see the progress being made in the Linux ecosystem, we remain committed to our core values of user-friendliness, privacy, and community-driven development.

The recent TAB election results have also been announced, and we're proud to see our community members being recognized for their contributions to the Linux Foundation. This is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our community, and we're honored to be a part of it.

As we continue to move forward, we're committed to staying true to our values and principles. We believe that a community-driven distribution should be free from lock-ins and nonsense, and we're working tirelessly to make that a reality.

We'd like to take this opportunity to thank our community members for their continued support and contributions. Your hard work and dedication are the driving force behind our progress, and we're grateful for your involvement.

Looking ahead, we're excited to see what the future holds for AcreetionOS. With a growing community and a clear vision for a user-friendly, privacy-focused Linux distribution, we're confident that we're on the right path. Stay tuned for more updates, and thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva
Co-Lead Developer, AcreetionOS
